description:
Start here for questions about a site's search traffic. Without site: a short summary of every site in the person's weekly site audit for last week, with each site's Google index, weekly crawl and search clicks, sites with changes first, ending with the site to ask about next; an account without the audit gets its site list to pick from. With site: the main report for that Search Console property, the overview plus each section's row count and top rows. With site and section: that section's rows; page sections also check their top 20 URLs live. Sections:
- overview: Site totals (clicks, impressions, CTR, position) against the previous period, by device, with the top pages and queries and their change, Google Analytics sessions for the same dates from the property whose web stream matches the site, clicks and impressions from image search, video search, the News tab, Discover, Google News and Google Lens and Circle to Search, and brand against not brand by the saved brand names and by Google’s own classification, and each market group saved in the business context.
- quick-wins: Query and page pairs at average positions 4 to 10 with a click-through rate below the site’s own curve for that position.
- low-ctr: Query and page pairs at average positions 1 to 4 with a click-through rate below the site’s own curve: titles and snippets to review with the person.
- striking-distance: Queries just outside the top positions, with impressions, for pages that already rank.
- second-page: Pages with an average position of 11 to 20 and their queries.
- content-decay: Query and page pairs that lost clicks against the previous period.
- cannibalization: Queries where more than one page of the site gets impressions, with each page’s share.
- traffic-drop: Daily clicks and impressions checked for a sudden change that lasted, with the date it started (else the last 7 days against the days before), and Google updates within 3 days of that date. Overlap is timing only, not cause.
- ai-queries: Queries with the shape of AI conversations and agent searches (replies such as "yes go on", follow-ups, agent prompts, search operators, a pronoun with nothing named, chat phrasing, ten or more words), with rewordings grouped into one question and its top page, impressions, clicks and position, and follow-up trails: follow-ups that reached one page on one day. A heuristic: Search Console does not mark AI Mode.
- image-search: Pages that show in Google Images, most image impressions first, with their clicks against the previous period; the top 20 are checked live for alt text, file names, background images and og:image.
- bing: Bing’s top queries from Bing Webmaster Tools with Google’s clicks, impressions and position for the same query beside them, and the same for pages; how many distinct queries each engine shows, and pages one engine shows that the other does not.
- issues: A list kept for the site between sessions: issues the striking-distance, low-ctr and quick-wins checks found (and the weekly crawl and Google index checks for an audited site), each with its id, the latest check and what it was marked (open, started with a pull request, fixed or ignored). A fixed page, or query on a page, gets its Search Console clicks and impressions for the 28 and 56 days from the day it was marked fixed against the same days before, once final data covers them. Asking for it runs those checks again. To mark issues, add mark and issues instead of section. The hosted server, and a CLI or local MCP linked to the account with seo login, keep the list with the account, for every site; an unlinked CLI or local MCP keeps it on this machine. A list the agent saved in the project before can be passed once as saved to carry it over.
- google-updates: One Google ranking update (core, spam and similar, from Google’s Search Status Dashboard) laid over the site’s Search Console data: clicks and impressions from the day it started against the same number of days just before (whole weeks, up to 28 days), whether that change is outside the site’s own movement in the 8 comparisons before it (a heuristic), and the folders, pages and queries that gained or lost most; brand against not brand (Google’s own classification when it covers the dates, else the saved brand names), devices, the market groups saved in the business context, the pages that moved on searches not about the brand, and the top Google Lens and Circle to Search pages. Early until a full week after the update finishes. The latest update by default; with end_date, the latest update that started on or before it. Timing only, not cause.
- progress: how far the site has come since its baseline, the first weekly point of Search Console numbers saved after the business context: brand, not brand and category searches, conversion pages with Google's index status and tracked searches, then every week since, and the tracked searches' Google positions and AI answers, first check against latest. end_date picks the last day compared.
- teardown: Only when the person asks for a teardown or a full written review of a site. The brief for writing one (what the site could win in Google and AI answers, where its search traffic lands today, and the changes in order of the growth they bring, each backed by numbers), the research calls to make in order, and the data SEO Skill has for it: clicks and impressions against the previous period, brand and non-brand clicks, clicks by folder and by page with Google Analytics key events, the conversion pages in the business context, and page-two searches with each page’s live title and main heading. Works for any domain: without a Search Console property it returns the brief and the research calls only. It spends no provider credit.
With site, mark and issues: records what happened to those issue ids (started, fixed, ignored, or open to undo) and runs no checks.

detail.description: summary first. rows: the next page of rows. full: every field as JSON.

fixed_on.description: Optional, with mark fixed: the day the change went live, YYYY-MM-DD, such as the day its pull request merged, when that was before today. Results are measured from it.

issues.description: With mark: issue ids from the issues section, comma-separated.

mark.description: Optional, with site and issues: started when a pull request with the change waits for review (note: its URL), fixed once the change is live, ignored only when the person says so, or open to undo.

note.description: Optional, with mark: why, in the person’s words, or the pull request URL for started.

offset.description: rows only: the first row to return.

saved.description: Optional, with section issues or mark: a list saved in the person's project before, such as .seo/issues.json, to carry over its marks once. This server keeps the list from then on.

section.description: Optional, needs site. Leave it out first; then ask for one section.

site.description: Leave it out for the summary of every site in the weekly site audit. Otherwise a Search Console property or site, such as sc-domain:example.com, https://example.com/ or example.com.

start_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; without end_date it runs to the latest final day.

name: seo_report
title: Search Console report
